lesson.title: Keep named options explicit
lesson.summary: Complete make_label(title, *, uppercase=False, **extras). The only permitted extra option is prefix, defaulting to empty text. Return prefix followed by title, uppercasing title only when uppercase is True. Unknown extra names raise ValueError. Inputs have the stated text/Boolean types; preserve prefix exactly.
explanation: A bare * in a function definition marks following named parameters as keyword-only. Callers must spell the option name instead of supplying its value by position.

```python
def caption(text, *, loud=False):
    return text.upper() if loud else text

print(caption("Hello", loud=True))
```
This returns HELLO. caption("Hello", True) is rejected because loud must be named. upper returns uppercase text.
**extras in a definition collects additional keyword arguments into a dictionary. It is different from *items, which collects positional arguments into a tuple.
For example, a call with prefix="Note: " stores that value under the key "prefix" in extras. extras.get("prefix", "") reads it or returns the supplied empty-text default when absent.
Accepting arbitrary extra names can hide spelling mistakes. In this exercise, loop over extras and raise ValueError if a key is not "prefix". The loop reads dictionary keys.
The task uppercases only title, not prefix. Choose the transformed title, then join prefix and that title with +. Do not add an extra separator: any desired space belongs to prefix.
Keyword-only arguments clarify call sites. They do not automatically validate the kinds of values, so this exercise states its accepted types.
The supplied __check_error helper is test infrastructure: it reports whether a sample call raises the expected error. Leave it unchanged; your task is make_label.

quiz.question: The function accepts **extras, but a caller types uprcase=True. Why reject that unknown name instead of silently ignoring it?
choices: Every keyword dictionary is automatically a syntax error.
It likely hides an intended option, leaving behavior different from the caller’s expectation.
Ignoring a spelling mistake always enables the intended option.
quiz.explanation: Collecting keywords does not validate their names. Explicit checking can expose a mistaken option.
